help: Physical hands: grabbing, weapon handling, recoil, scopes, grenades and the controller layout.

content.text: ROCK - Realistic Overengineered Character Kinetics - gives you physical hands in Fallout 4 VR. They collide with the world, pick things up, pull them from a distance, hold weapons by their grips, and use grenades and aid items by hand.

content.help: Opens the ROCK wiki in your browser. Take off the headset to read it on your monitor.
Walks you through ROCK's controls and main options. Mods Config steps aside until it closes.

content.text: <font color='#10FA78'>Grabbing:</font> Hold grip near an object to pick it up, or point at a far one and hold grip to bring it to you. Let go while moving to throw. Grab Direction and Far Grab Style are on the Interaction page.

<font color='#10FA78'>Weapons:</font> Grab a loose weapon by its firing grip to equip it. Hold the barrel or a front grip with your other hand to aim with both hands, and grab the firing grip with your other hand to switch hands. Weapon Equipping sets how grips take and let go.
<font color='#10FA78'>Two weapons:</font> Grab another weapon with your free hand to carry one in each hand. Each fires with its own trigger.
<font color='#10FA78'>Reload and scope:</font> Tap A on the firing hand to reload, hold it to look through the scope (X when you fire with your left hand).
<font color='#10FA78'>Grenades:</font> Hold B to draw a grenade into your hand, then throw it like a real one.
<font color='#10FA78'>Bipod:</font> Rest any part of your weapon on a surface and click the right stick to latch it there.

<font color='#10FA78'>Stash and use items:</font> Let go of an item behind your shoulder to put it in your inventory, and put a weapon away the same way. Touch a Stimpak to your body to inject it, and hold food or a drink at your mouth.
<font color='#10FA78'>Controls:</font> Every function and button can be moved on the Controls page. Index and Vive controllers get ROCK's SteamVR binding from the setup wizard.

pages.help: ROCK's developer options: tuning, debug drawing and logs.

content.text: Developer options tune ROCK and turn on its debug drawing and logs. ROCK_Developer.toml keeps only the options you change: Reset removes one, and the file goes when none remain. Changes show in the game as you make them.

content.help: How much ROCK writes to ROCK.log.

options.help: The basic log, for normal play.
More logs, to find a problem. Can cost frame time.
A lot of logs, every frame. Slows the game.
No log.

content.help: Gates advanced/tuning-only features not meant for normal play. Currently: pressing A while holding an object records/overwrites a saved grab offset for that object+hand. Saved offsets keep applying on future grabs regardless of this setting - it only gates recording new ones.

Emergency Disable Recoil ON: disables native VR recoil and kickback plus ROCK weapon/hand recoil, overriding every recoil profile. OFF: restores native recoil/kickback and the existing Immersive Recoil setting. Applies immediately, independently of Developer Mode. Does not change projectile spread.
Text format for each ROCK.log line.
Minimum time between repeated sampled diagnostic messages.

Writes each ROCK.log line to disk as it is logged. Off, the log is block buffered, so a freeze or a crash loses the last lines and every log ends mid-line. On, the tail survives, at one file write per line. Leave off unless you are chasing a hang.

Weapon visibility trace. Writes a VISIBILITY line to ROCK.log whenever the reason an equipped weapon would not render changes (a hidden node and who hid it, lost geometry, a stale bound, the weapon away from its hand, the scope), and a VISIBILITY tick once per second with the full state, the cell and the position. Independent from LogLevel. Walks the equipped weapons each frame; leave off for normal play.

Asynchronous performance profiler. Independent from LogLevel. When enabled, timing scopes stay on the frame path, but completed profiler windows are queued to a bounded background writer. Output goes to ROCK_Profiler.log, not ROCK.log. File formatting/writes are not done by grab, reload, physics, or frame update code. If the writer falls behind, profiler windows are dropped instead of stalling gameplay.
Number of frames per queued profiler window after warmup. Larger values reduce file traffic.
Startup/reload frames ignored before profiler windows are emitted.

Right-hand local position for the hidden grab authority proxy/seat point, in corrected palm proxy space. X follows the fingers, -Y moves into the palm face/skin, +Y moves to the back of the hand, and Z moves across the palm. This does not move the real palm/finger physics colliders.
Left-hand local position for the hidden grab authority proxy/seat point, in the same axes.
Controls whether ROCK weapon hulls collide with projectile/spell layers. False avoids self-collisions with modded projectile systems while aiming.

New casings ignore the firing weapon's generated colliders for this many simulation milliseconds. Positive values protect at least one physics step. Zero disables the grace period. Range: 0-500 ms. World contacts and native casing lifetime are preserved. Changes apply to new casings.

False: original convex fitting. True: bounded gap-preserving compounds. Changing this key rebuilds weapon colliders after a live settings reload. Compare with PerformanceProfilerEnabled: weaponColliderBuild/Create vs weaponGapColliderBuild/Create.
Seconds ROCK waits for the visual weapon tree to stay visible/stable before replacing generated hulls after weapon/mod swaps.
Maximum speed allowed when ROCK keyframes generated weapon hulls.

content.help: Far grabs pull the visual mesh point nearest the mesh's centre to the hand instead of the mesh point nearest the ray hit (a hit at selection range is aim noise, not grip intent). The arrival seat then settles the mesh onto the palm.

Long-object presentation during pull flight: rotates elongated props (brooms, bottles) so their mesh long axis lines up with the hand's thumb->pinky line before arrival. Flight-only; held objects are never rotated. Elongation is the RMS extent ratio between the mesh's dominant and second axis (compact objects ~1 skip presentation). Gain is proportional rad/s per rad of error.

content.text: Pull Presentation Angular Gain Per Second
Pull Presentation Max Angular Speed Radians Per Second
Pull Presentation Grip Axis Tilt Degrees
content.help: Tilts the presentation target off pure cross-palm Z toward fingers-forward +X, in degrees (0..45): the thumb occupies the pure-Z line, so the natural long-object hold sits a few degrees toward the fingertips. Applies to both the pull-flight servo and the force-grab seat alignment. This is an anatomical magnitude, not a signed rotation. Authored Z reverses its cross-palm direction between hands, but +X points toward the fingertips on both. ROCK resolves the live axes first, then tilts each signed Z axis toward its own +X, so one value has the same meaning for both hands.

content.text: Grab Seat Roll Min Second Elongation Ratio
content.help: Shape-classification gate shared by the flight presentation servo and the grab pose solver: sqrt(lambda2/lambda3) of the mesh PCA at or above this ratio marks a distinct flat face (plate class). The solver uses the class for its rod-only terms; plates keep their edge/corner holds (31 verified plate holds put the face normal 63 deg off the palm normal - edge holds are the intended grip, not an artifact).
Maximum scene-node depth used when scanning an object for physics bodies.
Shared dynamic-grab response for held objects and equipped weapon colliders. Higher tau increases positional recovery. Damping calms oscillation; angular response remains independent.
Angular shared-constraint motor response. Same idea as linear motor, but for rotation.
Contact and initial-attachment linear force ceiling. Free motion uses actual mass and Free Linear Acceleration.
Keeps the motor's effective mass finite for very light or unstable bodies.

content.text: Grab Max Force To Mass Ratio
content.help: Contact force per unit effective mass. This caps the contact ceiling for light objects.
Free-motion linear effort per unit effective driven mass, in Havok acceleration units. Contact keeps its separate ceiling.
Free-motion angular effort per unit maximum principal inertia. The grip lever adds capacity to oppose off-center linear effort; the native solver determines the applied torque.
Waits for a stable live hand transform before a force grab freezes its relation.
Time for grab force to ramp in after pickup.

content.help: Weapon response multipliers for both loose and equipped weapons. Max Force and Angular Force multipliers control contact and initial-attachment budgets. Free-motion budgets use actual mass, inertia, and the grip offset.

Native Scope Firing Grip Fallback Offset
content.help: Scope Anchor Without Optic Geometry Used only when a scoped weapon has no separate Scope or Sight part ROCK can measure, such as an optic modelled into the receiver. The scope view then starts at the firing hand's grip, moved by these values. Weapons with a measurable optic anchor on the optic and ignore these keys. Offsets are game units (70 = 1 metre) in the weapon's axes: X sideways, +Y toward the muzzle, Z up; all zero puts the anchor on the firing grip. Rotations are degrees added after the game's camera calibration: pitch about X, yaw about Z, roll about the muzzle axis. Position moves the activation point, camera and overlay together; rotation corrects the camera and overlay only. This key: the position. Each value: -100 to 100.

content.text: Native Scope Firing Grip Fallback Rotation
content.help: Rotation of the scope anchor used without optic geometry (see the offset above), in degrees: rot is [pitch, roll, yaw]. Each value: -180 to 180.

Scope Overlay Fine-tunes only the game's own world_scope.nif overlay. The activation camera stays on the resolved sight or firing-grip anchor, so these values do not change when the scope activates. All zero keeps automatic placement with the game's own model orientation and scale. Offsets are game units in the calibrated model frame; rotations are degrees: pitch about X, yaw about Z, roll about the optical Y axis. Tune one axis at a time; replacement scope meshes can use a reversed sign. This key: the position. Each value: -100 to 100.
Scope overlay rotation, in degrees: rot is [pitch, roll, yaw]. Each value: -180 to 180.
